 ORDER

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.350/2021, registered at P.S.- Katangi, District- Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC, 3,4,5L, 5J(ii),
6 of POCSO Act.
He is in detention since 19.09.2022.

As per the prosecution story, on 02.09.2021 prosecutrix's father lodged an FIR alleging that her 16 years 10 months old daughter who had left house around 4 P.M at the pretext of bringing powder from the shop, has not returned back.
Someone has kidnapped her daughter.
FIR was registered.
Almost after one year, prosecutrix was recovered and by that time she was 17 years 10 months old.
Applicant too is 18 years old boy.
At the time of recovery, prosecutrix was pregnant and now she has delivered a girl child.
She and her parents have already been examined before the trial Court.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is 18 years old young boy whereas at the time of commission of offence, prosecutrix was 17 years old.
They both were working as labourers at the same place and developed romantic love relationship.
They both left house for wages and entered into wedlock and now they have one offspring.
Prosecutrix and accused are from the lower strata of society.
As prosecutrix and her parents have already been examined before the trial Court, there is no possibility of influencing the evidence by the applicant.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant/accused be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the grant of bail to the present applicant.
Prosecutrix and her parents have already been examined before the trial Court.

Having taking into consideration their statements and statement of prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the present applicants/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant- Brijesh Nath be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction o f the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE anu Brijesh Nath vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148797265/
